title: Isandro and the Garden
premise: Wendell Thornbury, last apprentice of the Thornbury guild of gardeners who once kept the covenant between the human valley and the realm of Isandro, has spent her life in a valley where magic cannot follow — and where her forbidden gift lies dormant. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted and a dying stranger named Isandro stumbles into her garden, she learns the covenant was broken thirteen years ago, and that the moon's thirteenth turn will seal the realms apart forever, dooming both. Fleeing hunters led by her childhood friend Captain Rell, Wendell and Isandro cross a land where magic is returning in wild, dangerous ways, seeking the four lost keystones of the old covenant. Wendell discovers she is not merely a gardener's apprentice but the covenant's living heir, and that restoring it demands a sacrifice of memory — the price her guild was always meant to pay. At the climax she chooses to give up every memory of Isandro and her valley rather than let the realms bleed into ruin, and in the final chapter, with the covenant reforged and the hunt ended, Isandro plants a garden in the valley where magic can now live, waiting to see if love can outlast forgetting.
about_author: S. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former botanist who left research to write about the places memory and magic overlap. They live at the edge of a valley not unlike Wendell's, where they keep a garden that refuses to behave.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She tends the guild's walled garden, the last of its kind, and hides the faint shimmer her hands leave on living things. A crown herald posts a proclamation: all with the gift are to be surrendered. Emotional beat: quiet dread settling over a life she thought was safe.

chapters.title: Thirteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She questions her ailing grandmother, who admits the guild once served a covenant — and that something broke thirteen years ago, the night Wendell's parents vanished. Grandmother forbids her to ask more. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything she believed.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A wounded man with bark-like scarring collapses in the garden, calling her by a name no one uses. He carries a keystone that hums when she touches it. Emotional beat: recognition she cannot explain, and fear of her own answering power.

chapters.title: Isandro
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He wakes in the magicless valley, weakened, and explains he is the covenant's guardian from the other realm, sent to find its heir before the moon's thirteenth turn. He does not yet tell her the full cost. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Crown hunters reach the valley; among them is Captain Rell, her childhood friend, now sworn to the hunt. Grandmother burns the guild records and gives Wendell a seed-packet and a map. Emotional beat: betrayal of home by duty.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She and Isandro slip out through the old guild tunnels as hunters torch the garden. Crossing the boundary, magic floods back into her — overwhelming, beautiful, frightening. Emotional beat: grief and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: What the Gift Costs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He teaches Wendell to hold her gift without being consumed, and reveals that untrained gifted are exactly what the crown fears. Wendell's power answers to growing things — and to memory. Emotional beat: fragile trust forming.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They travel through a region the broken covenant has poisoned: crops that remember being forests, rivers that run backward. Villagers blame people like her. Emotional beat: seeing the cost of her guild's failure.

chapters.title: Captain Rell
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. He tracks them, torn between his oath and his memories of Wendell. His orders are explicit: the gifted are to be taken alive, for what the crown wants them for. Emotional beat: duty grinding against love.

chapters.title: The First Keystone
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In a drowned chapel they recover the first keystone, guarded by a memory-wraith that shows Wendell her parents' faces. She barely escapes with the stone and a fragment of a forgotten night. Emotional beat: hunger for the past.

chapters.title: The Crown's Purpose
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He learns the crown is harvesting the gifted to power a machine that will sever the realms permanently — the queen believes magic is the plague killing her kingdom. Emotional beat: the enemy is not evil but afraid.

chapters.title: A Market of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In a free town, gifted folk live openly in hiding. An old woman recognizes Wendell's guild sigil and gives her a warning: the covenant demands a price, and her guild knew it. Emotional beat: belonging, briefly, among the hunted.

chapters.title: Rell's Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Rell corners her alone and offers to falsify her death if she surrenders Isandro. She refuses, and he lets her go — a choice that will end him if discovered. Emotional beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Second Keystone
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The second keystone lies in the queen's own conservatory. Isandro's plan requires Wendell to use her gift to grow their way in. Emotional beat: Isandro's protectiveness curdling into dishonesty about the final price.

chapters.title: The Queen's Garden
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inside the palace conservatory she finds the crown's machine — caged gifted people, their magic siphoned, their memories stripped. Among them, a woman with her mother's hands. Emotional beat: horror and a terrible hope.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The woman does not know her, but a stolen memory surfaces: Wendell's parents did not abandon the covenant — they paid its price thirteen years ago, and it failed anyway. Emotional beat: the foundation of her identity cracking.

chapters.title: Flight from the Palace
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Their theft is discovered; Isandro frees what captives he can while Wendell takes the keystone. Rell covers their escape and is arrested for it. Emotional beat: escape bought with other people's sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Broken Bridge
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the border of Isandro's realm: a bridge of light severed thirteen years ago. The second keystone shows a vision of the covenant's making — and of the price, spoken plainly for the first time. Emotional beat: dread made certain.

chapters.title: The Price of the Covenant
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He confesses: reforging the covenant requires a memory-sacrifice from its heir — all memories tied to what she loves most. He has known since the garden. Wendell walks away from him into the dark. Emotional beat: love wounded by truth.

chapters.title: Alone Under the Ninth Moon
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She camps alone, furious, and the keystone shows her parents' full sacrifice — and that her mother left a message hidden in Wendell's own memory, sealed until she chose to look. Emotional beat: grief becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Message
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She unlocks the sealed memory: her mother's voice telling her the covenant can be reforged differently — shared willingly by two, rather than taken from one — but only if both choose it with open eyes. Emotional beat: a door where there was a wall.

chapters.title: The Third Keystone
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro, believing Wendell lost, goes alone to the third keystone in the marsh of forgetting and begins to lose his own memories to it. Wendell finds him not knowing her name. Emotional beat: reversal — she now remembers for both of them.

chapters.title: Remembering for Two
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She anchors Isandro with stories of their journey, rebuilding him memory by memory, and in the telling understands what the willing covenant would ask of her. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through narration.

chapters.title: The Queen's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Escaped and disgraced, Rell brings Wendell a proposition: the queen will halt the hunt and release the captives if the covenant's reforging includes sealing magic out of the human realm forever. Emotional beat: a mercy that is also an erasure.

chapters.title: What Wendell Refuses
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell refuses: a covenant built on exile is just the old broken one with a kinder face. Rell must choose — and he chooses her side, becoming a hunted traitor. Emotional beat: conviction over compromise.

chapters.title: The Fourth Keystone
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The fourth keystone is held by the wraith of the first guardian — Isandro's predecessor, and the one who broke the covenant thirteen years ago out of love for a human woman. Emotional beat: history repeating, and Isandro's fear that he will repeat it.

chapters.title: The First Guardian's Confession
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The wraith reveals she broke the covenant to save her human beloved from the memory-price — and the breaking is what killed the valley's magic and Wendell's parents. Love, withheld from the price, cost more. Emotional beat: warning and warning's opposite.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Moon
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Two turns remain. They reach the border bridge with all four keystones, but the crown's army arrives with the machine, and the queen herself comes to watch the realms be severed. Emotional beat: the clock running down.

chapters.title: The Machine Awakens
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The queen activates the severing; the caged gifted are drained to power it, and the border begins to tear. Isandro and Rell fight to reach the captives while Wendell reaches for the bridge. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, no clean sides.

chapters.title: The Queen's Memory
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell reaches the queen and, with the keystones, shows her the truth: the plague killing the kingdom is the covenant's breaking, not magic itself. The queen wavers but cannot stop the machine she has already fed. Emotional beat: empathy for the enemy, too late to be simple.

chapters.title: Rell's Stand
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell breaks the machine's core, knowing the backlash will take his memories of Wendell — the very thing the covenant asks of her. He does it laughing. Emotional beat: duty finally aligned with love, at ruinous cost.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Moon
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The bridge stands open for one night only. Wendell and Isandro stand before the four keystones and speak the covenant as her mother instructed: two who choose the price with open eyes. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness at the threshold.

chapters.title: What Wendell Gives
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The covenant takes its price — every memory of Isandro and of the valley's magic. Wendell pays it willingly, holding his hand, and the realms knit closed and whole around the wound. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible, quiet cost.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The moon completes its turn; the covenant holds; magic returns to the valley in balance. Isandro, remembering everything, crosses into the human realm with nothing but a seed-packet. Emotional beat: the asymmetry of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Gardener Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weeks later, Wendell rebuilds the guild garden with no memory of why her hands know these plants, or why she weeps at certain flowers. Rell visits; he remembers her but not their childhood. Emotional beat: grief without an object.

chapters.title: A Garden in the Valley
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro takes work as the valley's new gardener, planting a covenant-garden where magic can now live. He does not tell Wendell who he is. Emotional beat: patient, aching devotion.

chapters.title: Things the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Working beside the new gardener, Wendell's gift responds to him — plants lean toward them both when they're near. She begins to dream in a language she never learned. Emotional beat: memory outlasting memory.

chapters.title: The Name She Keeps Saying
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the covenant-garden's first bloom, Wendell finds her mother's message planted as a living thing — a flower that only grows when spoken to by name. She says 'Isandro,' and remembers everything. Emotional beat: love against duty, love against forgetting — love wins.

chapters.title: The Reforged Covenant
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell and Isandro renew the covenant openly, with the queen's blessing and the guild restored, its price now shared rather than stolen. Rell, memoryless but free, chooses to stay and learn the garden. Emotional beat: restoration with scars.

chapters.title: Isandro and the Garden
chapters.summary: Both POVs, braided. One year on: the garden blooms with plants from both realms, and the guild trains new gifted children in a valley where magic and memory can finally coexist. Wendell plants a seed her mother left and names it. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — and a future still growing.
